name: VXmodel
description: VXmodel is Creaform's scan-to-CAD software module inside its broader metrology software stack. Creaform's product materials and launch announcements describe it as the post-treatment stage between 3D scanning and downstream CAD, where users optimize meshes, extract sections and geometric entities, characterize freeform regions, and transfer the result into systems such as SOLIDWORKS, Inventor, or Fusion 360. That positioning makes it a strong representative of industrial reverse engineering as practiced on shop floors: the software does not just visualize scans, it prepares raw capture data for remodeling, additive workflows, and dimensional comparison. Relative to full standalone reverse-engineering suites, VXmodel is more modular and tightly coupled to Creaform's hardware and VXelements environment, but it still addresses the core scan-cleanup and geometry-preparation tasks needed before engineers create or validate CAD. The current status is deployed production.

name: ContextCapture
description: ContextCapture is Bentley Systems' reality-modeling engine for turning overlapping imagery and related survey inputs into reality meshes and digital context for engineering work. Bentley product pages describe it as part of the company's reality and spatial modeling stack, where users capture, process, manage, and share 3D mapping data from multiple sources for design, construction, and operations. Although the product is often framed for infrastructure and digital twins rather than mechanical reverse engineering, the core pipeline is directly relevant here: ContextCapture reconstructs large-scale geometry from photographs, calibrates cameras, and produces multiresolution 3D models that engineers can measure, stream, edit, and align with CAD or GIS environments. In this database it fits as a deployed production reconstruction tool that turns the physical world into mesh-based context ready for downstream model rebuilding and design integration.

name: Geomagic Design X
description: Geomagic Design X is Hexagon's flagship scan-to-CAD reverse engineering product. Hexagon's product and history pages describe it as the merger of Rapidform's parametric, history-based modeling with Geomagic's mesh-processing and surfacing stack, resulting in a system that turns scan data into editable, feature-based CAD. That combination is why the software remains central to industrial reverse engineering: users can fit primitives and surfaces to noisy mesh or point-cloud input, preserve a construction history, and hand results into downstream CAD systems rather than stopping at a static triangle mesh. While the product is commercial rather than academic, it embodies the workflow this file tracks most directly: converting real scanned parts into manufacturable parametric models for redesign, documentation, inspection handoff, and digital-twin creation. The current status is deployed production.

name: Artec Studio
description: Artec Studio is Artec 3D's scan-processing environment for turning raw handheld or desktop scanner captures into geometry that can be used for reverse engineering. Artec's reverse-engineering pages and release history show a progression from mesh cleanup and alignment toward explicit scan-to-CAD features, including primitive fitting, auto-surfacing improvements, CAD-oriented inspection tools, and streamlined export into downstream CAD systems such as Geomagic Design X and SOLIDWORKS. The newest releases also combine photogrammetry, texturing, and faster loading with reverse-engineering workflows, which makes the software a practical front end for scan-to-CAD pipelines even when the final parametric work happens elsewhere. In this database it belongs as a deployed production tool that bridges acquisition, reconstruction, and handoff from raw point-cloud or mesh data to CAD-ready geometry.

name: COLMAP
description: COLMAP is a 2021 open source from ETH Zurich. Sparse model of central Rome using 21K photos produced by COLMAP’s SfM pipeline.  Dense models of several landmarks produced by COLMAP’s MVS pipeline.  COLMAP is a general-purpose Structure-from-Motion (SfM) and Multi-View Stereo (MVS) pipeline with a graphical and command-line interface. It offers a wide range of features for reconstruction of ordered and unordered image collections. The software is licensed under the new BSD license. The latest source code is available at GitHub . COLMAP builds on top of existing works and when using specific algorithms within COLMAP, please also cite the original authors, as specified in the source code.

name: PIX4Dengine
description: PIX4Dengine is Pix4D's embeddable SDK and API for custom photogrammetry and 3D reconstruction workflows. Pix4D's developer and support documentation describes it as direct access to the company's camera calibration, dense point-cloud generation, DSM and DTM extraction, orthomosaic creation, and related processing algorithms, allowing teams to build their own scanning or reconstruction pipelines instead of using a fixed desktop product. Feature lists also highlight machine-learning point-cloud classification, AutoGCP marking, sky and water segmentation, LiDAR depth-point-cloud support, and Python integration, which makes the engine relevant to scan-to-CAD and scan-to-BIM toolchains that need programmable reconstruction rather than manual operator workflows. In this database it belongs as a deployed production foundation technology for converting imagery into structured 3D geometry and classified point clouds that downstream CAD or digital-twin systems can consume.

name: RealityCapture
description: RealityCapture is Epic Games' photogrammetry package for building 3D models from unordered photographs and laser scans. Official product pages describe a pipeline that automatically aligns images, calibrates cameras, reconstructs dense geometry, textures meshes, and supports survey outputs such as DSMs, DTMs, and georeferenced models. Although the software is widely used in media and digital-twin work, it is equally relevant to reverse engineering because it converts large image or scan collections into detailed polygonal models and point clouds that can later be simplified, measured, or remodeled into CAD. The product is not framed as a parametric CAD system, but it is a common front-end reconstruction engine in scan-to-model workflows where physical assets must be digitized quickly and accurately before downstream engineering cleanup. The current status is deployed production.

name: REcreate
description: REcreate is Hexagon's dedicated reverse-engineering environment for going from metrology scan to manufacturable CAD in a single workspace. Hexagon's launch materials and product pages describe a workflow that moves from point cloud to mesh to surface to solid while preserving an interactive modeling environment instead of forcing engineers to jump across separate scanning, meshing, and CAD tools. That positioning makes REcreate unusually direct for this file: it is explicitly designed to streamline conversion of measured parts into manufacturing-ready digital models and digital twins. Compared with general photogrammetry tools, REcreate focuses much more on the reconstruction and remodeling stage, where operators need editable surfaces and solids rather than just a textured mesh. The current status is deployed production, although Hexagon notes that the product now sits inside its broader DESIGNER offering.

name: 3DF Zephyr
description: 3DF Zephyr is a 2023 commercial product from 3Dflow. 3DF Zephyr allows you to automatically reconstruct 3D models from photos. Zephyr is the perfect tool to capture reality: a complete photogrammetry software. is the photogrammetry software solution by 3Dflow to automatically reconstruct 3D models from photos: deal with any 3D reconstruction and scanning challenge. No matter what camera sensor, drone or laser scanner device you are going to use. From the camera orientation to the texture generation phase. It is grouped here as a image to cad system because it takes image input and produces mesh output. The current status is best described as deployed production.

name: Cyclone 3DR
description: Cyclone 3DR is a 2023 commercial product from Leica Geosystems. Leica Cyclone 3DR is a deliverable creation tool for point cloud software for meshing, inspection and reporting. Transform point cloud data with Leica Cyclone 3DR's efficient workflows and tools, enabling intuitive data analysis, modelling, and visualisation in the AEC, Surveying, and Plant industries Professional results in a fraction of the time Leica Cyclone 3DR is a powerful software solution that transforms point cloud data into accessible 3D models and actionable deliverables, leveraging automation and AI classification tools. Where most software will focus on a single workflow to create a specialised deliverable, Cyclone 3DR includes a range of adaptable tools for inspection, modelling and meshing that can be leveraged to create an assortment of 3D deliverables and reports.

name: FARO BuildIT Construction
description: FARO BuildIT Construction is a 2023 commercial product from FARO. FARO BuildIT Construction Software is a complete design software solution for continuous construction verification Use FARO BuildIT Construction Software to save time and money by validating construction element’s quality in prefabrication and on-site against BIM models and local standards. BuildIT Construction measures aspects such as floor flatness, levelness and wall plumbness, while also enabling accurate comparisons to original design files and BIM documentation. As-built positional changes to floors, steel beams, walls, columns, windows and doors can also be measured. With FARO WebShare, all project stakeholders can view the 3D analysis results from BuildIT Construction through a web browser for collaboration, eliminating the need for time-consuming file imports. The software also seamlessly integrates with FARO Focus Laser Scanners , Laser Trackers and Tracer Laser Projectors . Maximize quality assurance and quality control by evaluating projects with real-time comparisons against CAD/BIM designs and local standards using 3D scan data. Plus, automate processes such as 3D data importing and reporting. See all construction quality control applications >

name: FlexScan3D
description: FlexScan3D is Polyga's scanner-control and post-processing environment for structured-light 3D capture and downstream reverse engineering. Polyga's product pages describe a full workflow that captures scans, aligns and merges multiple views, edits meshes, fills holes, performs deviation analysis, and exports digital models into downstream applications such as reverse engineering, metrology, and visualization tools. That makes the software a practical scan-to-model front end rather than only a device driver: it is the stage where raw measurements become clean, merged geometry that engineers can use as the basis for CAD rebuilding or dimensional comparison. Because the system includes measurement and benchmarking alongside mesh processing, it sits close to the boundary between capture, inspection, and reconstruction. The current status is deployed production, with Polyga positioning it as the control center for its professional scanners and downstream reverse-engineering workflows.

name: RangeVision PRO
description: RangeVision PRO is a 2023 commercial product from RangeVision. Products Get accurate 3D models for your production task Fast 3D inspection and obtaining accurate 3D data without contact to catch deviation with CAD Mesh distance control allows to visualize the deviations in the form of a colour map and take measurements at each individual point of the inspected 3D mesh. It is grouped here as a cad reconstruction system because it takes point cloud input and produces mesh output. The current status is best described as deployed production.

name: Trnio
description: Trnio is a 2023 commercial product from Trnio. Crisp, detailed 3D scans in the palm of your hand. Our iOS 3D scanner apps combines ARKit and LiDar to produce crystal clear captures, and adds effortless editing and exporting capabilities. Capture anything from faces to food to buildings. Scan with confidence! First and foremost, we want to extend our heartfelt thanks to every Trnio and Trnio Plus user. The enthusiasm you've all exhibited, along with the fantastic work you've created by scanning, has truly been inspiring. After much consideration, we have decided it's time to retire both the Trnio and Trnio Plus apps. For safeguarding your work, we strongly recommend you download any scans you wish to preserve. We are currently devising a solution that will allow you to download all your data comprehensively in the upcoming weeks. Thank you once again for being an integral part of our journey. Stay tuned for our future endeavours.

name: Geomagic Wrap
description: Geomagic Wrap is Hexagon's mesh and point-cloud processing product for reverse-engineering workflows that start with raw scan data but do not yet need full parametric remodeling. Hexagon positions the software as a fast path from scan to usable 3D model by combining scanner connectivity, large point-cloud handling, mesh editing, scripting, and NURBS surfacing tools in one environment. That matters for engineering practice because many scan-to-CAD pipelines need an intermediate stage where meshes are cleaned, aligned, decimated, patched, and surfaced before engineers rebuild or inspect the part in a downstream CAD system. Compared with Design X, Wrap sits earlier in the reconstruction workflow and emphasizes scan processing plus surface creation rather than end-to-end parametric feature history. The current status is deployed production and actively maintained in Hexagon's Geomagic portfolio.

name: Polycam
description: Polycam is a 2024 commercial product from Polycam. Capture reality and create digital twins, on iPhone, iPad, Android and web. Document, measure, design with spatial AI. Generate floor plans, 3D models, and drone mapping. Capture spaces and interiors — your own digital reference perfect for any project. Fast documentation and measurement. Create instantly shareable 3D models of any object. Generate customizable 2D floor plans before leaving the site. It is grouped here as a image to cad system because it takes image input and produces mesh output. The current status is best described as deployed production.

name: PolyWorks
description: PolyWorks is a 2024 commercial product from InnovMetric. Empowering the digital transformation​ of your 3D measurement processes. Contact us to initiate your digital journey. Discover the story behind our mission, our people, and our passion for innovation This video takes you beyond our solution—inside PolyWorks USA, an InnovMetric group company—to show how we're helping manufacturers around the world transform the way they work. From global partnerships to local impact, see how our commitment to empowering people drives our approach to delivering meaningful results. Supporting all your industrial manufacturing organization’s 3D measurement processes

name: Revopoint Revo Scan
description: Revopoint Revo Scan is a 2024 commercial product from Revopoint. Revopoint’s portable 3D scanner delivers high-precision, professional scanning for 3D printing, modeling, and industrial use—ideal for capturing accurate, detailed models. Engineered for Measurement : High-Performance Wireless 3D Scanner Portable Blue Laser 3D Scanners for Small to Medium Workpieces Optical Tracking 3D Scanner for Marker-free Scans It is grouped here as a cad reconstruction system because it takes point cloud input and produces mesh output. The current status is best described as deployed production.

name: SHINING 3D EXModel
description: SHINING 3D EXModel is a 2024 commercial product from SHINING 3D. EXModel, seamlessly convert 3D scans to CAD, AI powered tools for fast product 3D reverse engineering design. EXModel is a powerful gateway that simplifies CAD modeling, from 3D scanning to manufacturing. It provides a comprehensive set of tools that enable you to transform a mesh into a professional-quality CAD solid model in just a few simple steps. The EXModel is seamlessly integrated with SHINING 3D Scanning software. After scanning, you can transfer the mesh data to EXModel with a single click, making the transition from scan to design even easier. EXModel's mesh editing tools are simple to use and make it easy to reduce data size while maintaining accuracy. You can easily fill in holes and remove mesh outliers to easily create watertight meshes for 3D printing or reverse engineering.

name: Geomagic for SOLIDWORKS
description: Geomagic for SOLIDWORKS is Hexagon's integrated scan-to-CAD add-in for users who want reverse-engineering tools inside the native SOLIDWORKS environment rather than in a separate standalone application. Hexagon and the current SOLIDWORKS partner materials describe it as a complete scan-to-SOLIDWORKS workflow with scanner input, mesh and point-cloud processing, real-time deviation analysis, and direct rebuilding of usable CAD in the host system. That makes the product strategically important for engineering teams that already standardize on SOLIDWORKS and need to convert physical parts into editable design models without adding a separate modeling workflow for every operator. Compared with general scan processors, it is more tightly coupled to parametric reconstruction and CAD handoff inside a mainstream mechanical CAD stack. The current status is deployed production as part of Hexagon's Geomagic portfolio.

name: XTract3D
description: XTract3D is Polyga's reverse-engineering add-in for SOLIDWORKS that uses imported scan data as a live reference for building parametric models. Polyga's product pages describe a deliberately manual but efficient workflow: engineers slice dense meshes or point clouds, fit and snap sketches against cross sections, and rebuild stable CAD features directly inside a familiar CAD environment instead of switching between separate scanning and modeling packages. That approach makes XTract3D a useful complement to fully automatic reconstruction systems, especially when operators need control over how noisy or partial scan data is interpreted. Because it works natively in SOLIDWORKS and is marketed specifically as scan-to-CAD, it belongs in this file as a deployed production tool for practical reverse engineering of mechanical parts from scan data to editable CAD.

name: Autodesk ReCap Pro
description: Autodesk ReCap Pro is Autodesk's reality-capture product for converting photographs and laser scans into point clouds, meshes, and as-built digital models that downstream Autodesk tools can consume. Autodesk's product and help pages position it as the capture and management layer for complex 3D scanning and photogrammetry projects, with automated registration, scan stitching, cleanup, cloud workflows, and feature extraction for engineering use. That means ReCap Pro often occupies the front of a scan-to-design pipeline rather than the final parametric reconstruction stage: users organize and register raw field data, create point clouds or meshes, then hand the results into Revit, Civil 3D, or other CAD/BIM systems for modeling and documentation. In this database it fits as a deployed production bridge between reality capture and CAD reconstruction, especially for as-built and existing-conditions workflows.

name: QUICKSURFACE
description: QUICKSURFACE is KVS Ltd's dedicated scan-to-CAD system for turning meshes and point clouds into editable engineering geometry. The vendor's official site and company history describe it as a standalone product introduced in 2019 after earlier scan-processing and reverse-engineering work around ModelMaker, KUBE, and Mesh2Surface. Current product materials emphasize a scan-first workflow built for noisy real-world data: import meshes or point clouds, align scans, extract primitives and curves, mix freeform surfacing with parametric modeling, and export stable STEP or IGES data for downstream CAD and manufacturing tools. That focus makes the product notable in this database because it is neither a general-purpose CAD system nor just a scanner utility; it is a purpose-built bridge from physical capture to production-ready geometry. The current status is deployed production with active yearly releases and OEM partnerships.

name: Scan2CAD
description: Scan2CAD is one of the canonical benchmark resources for scan-to-CAD alignment. The CVPR 2019 project and paper describe a paired dataset built from 1,506 ScanNet RGB-D scans and 14,225 ShapeNet CAD models, with 97,607 manually annotated keypoint correspondences linking clean CAD objects to noisy real-world scan geometry. The associated method predicts 9DoF alignments between database CAD models and objects observed in indoor scans, which made the benchmark central to later work on retrieval, pose estimation, and scene reconstruction with editable object geometry. For this database, Scan2CAD matters less as a production tool than as infrastructure: it turned reverse-engineering style alignment into a measurable machine-learning problem with shared data and evaluation. The status is released benchmark and it remains a common reference point for scan-to-CAD research.

name: Supervised Fitting of Geometric Primitives to 3D Point Clouds
description: This CVPR 2019 paper introduced the Supervised Primitive Fitting Network, or SPFN, as a learned alternative to classic multi-primitive RANSAC pipelines for turning point clouds into structured geometric descriptions. The official Adobe Research summary explains that SPFN first predicts per-point primitive memberships, normals, and types, then uses a differentiable model-estimation stage to recover primitive parameters instead of directly regressing shape coefficients in one shot. The authors report a significant improvement over both strong RANSAC baselines and direct neural prediction on a benchmark of ANSI mechanical component models, which is why the work matters for scan-to-CAD: primitive decomposition is often the intermediate representation needed before generating editable engineering geometry. The status is research prototype, but the method remains a widely cited reference for learned primitive extraction from noisy point clouds.
